rule.name: App Transport Security Allows Arbitrary Loads
rule.rule_desc: The checked source contains a transport-security exception, insecure endpoint, or certificate-validation configuration. Resolve the effective policy and the connections it governs.
rule.vuln_desc: An attacker on the network may read or alter affected traffic if sensitive data travels over cleartext or the connection accepts an untrusted server. Normal HTTPS endpoints and correctly implemented validation do not establish exposure.
rule.developer: Use HTTPS with normal certificate-chain and hostname verification. Remove permissive production callbacks and broad transport exceptions; restrict any justified exception to a documented, non-sensitive endpoint.
rule.reviewer: Review Info. plist ATS entries and validate that all exceptions are justified and limited. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Insecure URL Scheme Registration
rule.rule_desc: The code handles a link, redirect, or externally selected navigation target. Validate the effective destination and any action triggered by the receiving handler.
rule.vuln_desc: A crafted destination or link may direct users to a phishing site, leak URL-carried secrets, or trigger unauthorized operations if routing trusts external parameters without the required access checks.
rule.developer: Allowlist schemes, hosts, paths, and operations. Validate parsed link parameters, avoid credentials in URLs, and require authentication and authorization before sensitive actions.
rule.reviewer: Assess deep-link handlers for authentication, authorization, and input validation. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Application Queries Schemes Broad Allowlist
rule.rule_desc: Application configuration permits querying a broad set of URL schemes associated with other applications.
rule.vuln_desc: Collecting the resulting application-presence information may reveal aspects of a user’s installed applications or behavior if the collection exceeds the authorized feature.
rule.developer: Limit query schemes to required integrations, avoid collecting an unnecessary application inventory, and document the purpose and handling of resulting information.
rule.reviewer: Ensure scheme allowlist entries are minimal and justified. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Keychain Accessibility Too Permissive
rule.rule_desc: The application stores sensitive values or configures protection for persistent data. Determine the actual storage location, backup policy, and lock-state access restrictions.
rule.vuln_desc: An actor with access to unprotected application files, backups, or overly broad keychain access may recover credentials or private records and use them outside the intended trust boundary.
rule.developer: Use the platform credential or key store for secrets and appropriate authenticated encryption and file protection for private records. Minimize stored data, backup exposure, and lock-state accessibility.
rule.reviewer: Check keychain storage options for least-privilege accessibility settings. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: WebView JavaScript Enabled for Dynamic Content

rule.vuln_desc: Attacker-controlled web content may execute in a trusted context or invoke native operations, exposing session data or application privileges when isolation and per-operation checks are insufficient.

rule.name: UIPasteboard Write with Sensitive Data
rule.rule_desc: The application reads the shared clipboard or pasteboard. Review whether the read follows an explicit paste action and whether the returned content enters logs, storage, or network requests.
rule.vuln_desc: Passwords, payment details, or other private content copied from another application could be collected or disclosed if clipboard reads occur without user intent or the content is sent to an unauthorized recipient. Platform access restrictions and the actual handling of the data determine exposure.
rule.developer: Read clipboard content only for an explicit user paste action. Process only the value needed for that action, avoid logging or transmitting it unnecessarily, and respect platform clipboard access restrictions.
rule.reviewer: Confirm that any pasteboard writes containing sensitive data set localOnly and a short expiration. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: evaluateJavaScript with Potentially User-Controlled Input
rule.rule_desc: The code invokes an interpreter, process, dynamic expression, or template-execution mechanism. Trace executable selection and evaluated content to their trust boundaries.
rule.vuln_desc: If an attacker controls interpreted syntax or the operation selected, code or commands may run with the application’s privileges, allowing data theft, state changes, or service disruption.
rule.developer: Replace externally influenced evaluation with fixed operations and data-only inputs. Use separate argument arrays for processes, allowlist permitted operations, and keep untrusted text out of executable templates or expressions.
rule.reviewer: Inspect the script string construction to determine if user-controlled data flows in without sanitization or encoding. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Debug Logging in Production Code Paths
rule.rule_desc: The code writes diagnostic data or exposes detailed errors. Establish the values emitted, production configuration, and recipients of the output.
rule.vuln_desc: Readers of exposed diagnostics may obtain credentials, private records, internal paths, or implementation details that enable account misuse or targeted attacks.
rule.developer: Keep sensitive values and detailed errors out of user-facing responses and routine logs. Redact before emission, restrict diagnostic access, and verify production logging configuration.
rule.reviewer: Check logging behavior for production builds and sensitive-data exposure. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Push Notification Entitlement Enabled
rule.rule_desc: The application declares push-notification support. This is a capability declaration rather than evidence of insecure notification handling.
rule.vuln_desc: Private notification payloads may be disclosed on lock screens or through an unauthorized recipient, and crafted notification actions may affect state if handler authorization is inadequate.
rule.developer: Keep secrets out of notification payloads, verify device-token ownership and delivery recipients, and require authorization before executing sensitive notification actions.
rule.reviewer: Review push handlers for sensitive data exposure and authorization checks. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.rule_desc: The application renders web content, executes scripts, or exposes a native messaging interface. Resolve navigation trust, origin isolation, and validation at the native boundary.
rule.vuln_desc: Attacker-controlled web content may execute in a trusted context or invoke native operations, exposing session data or application privileges when isolation and per-operation checks are insufficient.
rule.developer: Restrict navigation and message origins to required trusted sources. Avoid dynamic script construction, minimize native bridge methods, validate message inputs, and authorize sensitive native operations.
rule.reviewer: Confirm all web view usage has been migrated to WKWebView. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Insecure Random Number Generation
rule.rule_desc: The checked source uses a random generator, cryptographic primitive, or initialization value whose suitability depends on its security purpose and inputs.
rule.vuln_desc: Predictable secrets or unsuitable cryptographic parameters may enable credential guessing, reveal plaintext, or weaken integrity when used to protect security-sensitive data. Non-security hashes and identifiers do not establish this condition.
rule.developer: Use a cryptographically secure generator for secrets and modern purpose-appropriate cryptography. Use unique nonces, protected keys, and a vetted password-hashing scheme where passwords are stored.
rule.reviewer: Verify security-critical random values use SecRandomCopyBytes or CryptoKit equivalents. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Hardcoded Cryptographic Key or Secret
rule.rule_desc: The checked source or build configuration embeds potentially sensitive credential or key material. Determine whether it is active and whether it reaches distributed artifacts or logs.
rule.vuln_desc: A party who can read exposed source, artifacts, configuration, or logs may recover active secrets and access the protected service or decrypt data with the secret owner’s privileges.
rule.developer: Remove active secrets from source and build layers, rotate exposed values, and load replacements through a restricted secret-management facility. Use narrowly privileged, short-lived credentials.
rule.reviewer: Verify no long-lived secrets or keys are embedded as string literals. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Certificate Pinning Using Leaf Certificate Hash Only
rule.rule_desc: The code configures an additional server or update authenticity mechanism. Confirm the intended trust boundary and effective verification policy.
rule.vuln_desc: If the intended authenticity check is absent or can be bypassed, a party controlling an otherwise accepted certificate or update source may impersonate a trusted endpoint or supply unauthorized code. Pinning absence alone does not prove broken TLS.
rule.developer: Document the required authenticity policy, verify signatures or the intended certificate or public-key pins, and test key rotation and failure behavior without disabling normal platform validation.
rule.reviewer: Confirm the pinning implementation compares public key hashes (SPKI), not raw certificate data. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.
